previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for evaluation of leaking from his left nephrostomy tube, which began after a recent replacement during a prior hospitalization. He has a complex medical history including T12 paraplegia, chronic kidney disease stage IV, neurogenic bladder, and recurrent urinary infections. Imaging revealed a stricture at the ureteropelvic junction and near the ileostomy anastomosis, contributing to the leakage. The nephrostomy tube was successfully exchanged with a modified stent, resolving the leak. He was found to have asymptomatic bacteriuria with E. coli, which did not require treatment. His chronic metabolic acidosis improved with an increased dose of sodium bicarbonate, and his previously noted toxic metabolic encephalopathy resolved. Nephrology was consulted, and a follow-up appointment was scheduled to discuss future dialysis planning. He remained stable, with no signs of active infection or complications, and was discharged home in improved condition.

was discharged on clindamycin 300 mg PO Q8H with end date ___. He remained afebrile with no leukocytosis during 
hospitalization. 

Note: given that Mr. ___ removed the toe nails on toes four

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to ___ after 
experiencing back pain and fever. You underwent a CT scan of 
your abdomen and pelvis which did not reveal any infectious 
source. You were seen by the Urologists who did not believe you 
had an active infection relating to the ileo-conduit or your 
kidneys.  

However, you were noted to have redness and warmth on your right 
foot. You noted that you had bumped this foot prior to this 
presentation. Based on the presentation, you were seen by wound 
care who believed the redness was consistent with a skin 
infection called cellulitis. In order to treat this, you were 
started on an antibiotic called linezolid. Unfortunately, you 
developed an allergic reaction to this medication, and the 
medication was stopped. Linezolid should now be included in your 
list of allergies. 

To treat the cellulitis you were started on a different 
antibiotic called clindamycin. You responded well to the 
clindamycin with improvement of the erythema and warmth of the 
foot. You also noted your appetite was improving after starting 
the medication. Please continue to take the clindamycin 300 
milligrams EVERY 8 HOURS with end date ___.  

The back pain was likely secondary to muscle spasms. These may 
come and go throughout the days. Please follow-up with your 
primary care physician to discuss the back pain. 

A urine culture of yours did show mixed flora within the urine 
which is consistent with contamination rather than a true 
urinary tract infection. As a result, this did not require 
antibiotic treatment.

During hospitalization it was also noted that you had 
significant fluid output from your urostomy bag. Please continue 
to stay very hydrated throughout the day. 

Please also stay on a very low potassium diet given your kidney 
dysfunction. 

To treat your high blood pressure, you were re-started on 
amlodipine 2.5 milligrams by mouth daily. Please discuss with 
your primary care physician if this medication requires an 
adjustment to the dose to better control your blood pressure. 

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your 
hospitalization! We wish you all the ___!

Sincerely,
Your ___ Care Team
